title: Massachusetts blocks Holtec from discharging Pilgrim water
summary: In 2024, the Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection (MassDEP) denied Holtec International’s application to release treated water into Cape Cod Bay from the Pilgrim nuclear power plant site as decommissioning work continues. Holtec appealed that decision, and on Tuesday, MassDEP announced that it has dismissed the appeal, leaving Holtec—for now—with fewer options for how to deal with the up to 1.1 million gallons of water it seeks to discharge.

title: U.K. regulators plan “radical reforms,” begin Xe-100 assessment
summary: Earlier this year, the United Kingdom released plans intended to “fundamentally reshape the regulatory landscape” of the nuclear industry and speed nuclear deployment. A policy paper, “Building Our Nuclear Nation,” was released in March 2026, and that same month, then chancellor Rachel Reeves sent a letter to the U.K. Office for Nuclear Regulation that posed five questions on how ONR and other regulators planned to adapt.

title: The whole picture: BNL researchers combine CT technologies to study nuclear materials
summary: Often, multiple tests need to be performed to make an accurate diagnosis. This can be the case for illnesses, a strange rattle in a car, computer troubleshooting—and examining nuclear materials. Rather than wait the days or even weeks it would take to run such tests one after the other, a team at Brookhaven National Library has developed a way to get multiple images concurrently, shortening the testing time to just hours.
